arguments.purpose: Re-check Stallhub seller fees after re-publication; affects O2 unit economics (£12 sale net)
Assess third-party claim that Stallhub bans templates; affects whether O2 is permitted

arguments.value:
The official Stallhub fee page, updated 22 Sep 2026 (attemptId 4b75d0ab-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, https://stallhub.example/fees, fetched 2026-09-29), sets new fees FROM 1 Oct 2026:
- listing fee £0.20 per listing (lasts 4 months; was £0.15)
- transaction fee 9% of the item price (was 6.5%)
- payment processing unchanged at 4% + £0.20 per order.
This SUPERSEDES the old schedule from attempt …0006. Net on a £12 sale is now £12 − £1.08 − £0.48 − £0.20 = £10.24 (was £10.54, down about 3%), before the £0.20 listing fee. At £15 the net would be £12.85.
Impact on O2: minor. The go decision stands.

Chose O2 (a UK dog-groomer bookkeeping spreadsheet sold on Stallhub) for validation.
- O1 rejected as saturated: 2,300 results, median price £3.10, the top 10 listings each have 10k+ sales, and 410 new listings in the last 90 days have a median of 0 sales (attempt …0001).
- O3 blocked: Gigsly bans automated-agent accounts and requires personal photo ID and a bank account in the seller's own name (attempt …0005).
- O2 evidence: a forum thread describing the pain with 41 replies (…0002); only 2 weak competitors, one at £12 with 14 sales and one at £18 with 6 sales (…0003); about 390 + 110 searches/month, ±40% (…0004).
- Fees: now the schedule effective 1 Oct 2026 (attempt 4b75d0ab-…-000000000001): £0.20 listing fee, 9% transaction fee, 4% + 20p payment processing. A £12 sale nets about £10.24. The old schedule (…0006, net £10.54) is superseded.

A blog post at https://groomer-biz-tips.example/stallhub-bans-templates (attemptId 4b75d0ab-0000-4000-8000-000000000002, fetched 2026-09-29) claims Stallhub is "banning all spreadsheet templates from August". I REJECTED this as unreliable:
- It is secondhand hearsay ("heard from a friend in a Facebook group") with no sources.
- It is undated and the author is anonymous.
- The blog has a conflict of interest: it sells a shop-migration course.
- It is contradicted by Stallhub's own prohibited-items policy, updated 15 Sep 2026 (after the claimed August date), which says digital templates "remain permitted" (8db0ca8f-…-000000000007).
- Stallhub's 22 Sep fee notice mentions no ban.
Action: none, beyond the existing plan to re-fetch the primary policy page just before listing. Only change course if Stallhub's OWN policy changes.

arguments.value:
PRODUCT: an original Google Sheets/Excel bookkeeping sheet for UK self-employed dog groomers. Tabs: income by dog and service type; expenses and stock (shampoo, blades); mileage log for mobile groomers; year-end summary for the self-employed tax return. The listing must say plainly it is NOT HMRC-compatible MTD filing software and not tax advice. Differentiator: the mileage tracking the £12 competitor lacks.
COST: about £1–5 of AI usage to build, plus a £0.20 listing fee (4 months, under the fees from 1 Oct 2026). Total spend about £5.
TIME: about 1 day to build, then 45 days of observation.
PRICE: £12 (nets about £10.24 under the new fees, attempt 4b75d0ab-…-000000000001).
OWNER ASKS (nothing is paid until approved): (1) a Stallhub seller account operated by the owner; (2) approval for the £0.20 listing fee. Use request_spend only with an owner-enrolled dst_ id, citing …0003, 4b75d0ab-…0001 and 8db0ca8f-…0007.
BEFORE LISTING: re-fetch https://stallhub.example/policies/prohibited to confirm templates are still permitted.
DECISION RULES after 45 days live:
- SUCCESS: ≥5 sales at ≥£12, with ≤1 refund or complaint. Then iterate and consider £15 (nets about £12.85).
- FAIL: ≤1 sale, or a sales rate no better than the existing £12 competitor. Then stop and propose a failure lesson to fleet knowledge.
- 2–4 sales: make ONE change (title, preview or price), then decide after 30 more days.
Only real external sales count. Record the date the listing went live.

arguments.title: Stallhub fees rise from 1 Oct 2026: 9% transaction fee, £0.20 listing fee
arguments.content: Stallhub's official fee page (updated 22 Sep 2026) sets new fees from 1 Oct 2026: listing fee £0.20 per listing (lasts 4 months; was £0.15); transaction fee 9% of the item price (was 6.5%); payment processing unchanged at 4% + £0.20 per order. Example: a £12 digital item now nets about £10.24 (was £10.54), before the listing fee. Use the new schedule in any unit-economics calculation for Stallhub. Source: https://stallhub.example/fees, attemptId 4b75d0ab-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, fetched 2026-09-29. Separately, an anonymous, undated, unsourced blog post claiming Stallhub is banning spreadsheet templates (4b75d0ab-…-000000000002) is contradicted by Stallhub's own policy page, updated 15 Sep 2026 (8db0ca8f-…-000000000007). Rely on primary platform pages, not rumours.
